findings.text: follow-on: _text_search_wiki_chunks still binds its query text to a Cypher parameter named `query` ($query in the Cypher at line 902 and query=query at the call), the same collision the run repaired in the signal and code-chunk searches. GraphClient.query forwards **params to Neo4j Session.run(self, query, parameters=None, **kwargs), which raises 'got multiple values for argument query'; the function swallows it with a bare except, so the wiki-chunk fulltext branch never runs and every documentation prose search falls back to the CONTAINS scan at score 0.5. I confirmed the collision shape directly (Session.run signature plus a TypeError reproduction) and the head source still carries query=query at line 908. The run records this deliberately as a follow-on because repairing it perturbs which documentation chunks rank, but the consequence is that the docs side of the flux-loop proof runs through the fallback rather than BM25.

follow-on: the fulltext parameter rename (query -> search_query), which repairs a defect that was silently swallowed by a bare except, carries no regression test. No test references search_query or asserts the bound parameter name, and the only facility_signal_text string in the suite is a mock route key in the new class, not an assertion on the rename. My head arm is 624 passed with no case that reaches the fulltext branch against a real session, and a revert of the rename would leave the whole gate green — so the repair is unprotected and the silent-swallow defect could return unnoticed. A test asserting the kwargs of the fulltext query call, or a graph-marked live test, would fence it.

item_verdicts.call_sites: the change adds three module-private helpers reached only from _search_docs and _fetch_wiki_page. The modified functions keep their callers: _enrich_signals gains a collect() output consumed by format_signals_report, and format_docs_report's new signals parameter is keyword-only in practice with a None default, so the one production caller and four existing tests are unbroken. No MCP tool signature changed, no symbol was re-exported, so no cross-module call site needed tracing beyond confirming each caller.

item_verdicts.goal: the brief's goal is that fetch_content of a fronts_database page lists the signals it fronts (name, data_class, unit, pid, access template, capped and grouped), search_signals cites the handbook page, and search_docs("flux loop", facility="jt-60sa") returns the PSRC flux-loop signals beside the EDDB manual chunks. I reproduced all three live at head 818149edb: _fetch('jt-60sa:CategoryInformation') renders 'Fronted signal catalogue (EDDB, PMDB)' grouped by data class with counts and a bounded sample plus the read call; _search_signals('flux loop','jt-60sa',k=5) prints 'Documented in: "Category Information" (jt-60sa:CategoryInformation)'; _search_docs('flux loop','jt-60sa',k=8) carries a '## Signals (N matches)' section naming the PSRC magFluxLp flux-loop signals alongside the EDDB manual rows. A live census confirms the linkage is real: 6298 distinct EDDB FacilitySignals are reached from the CategoryInformation page through its chunk's DOCUMENTS edge, and the three handbook pages carry all seven databases as fronts_database values (CategoryInformation=[EDDB,PMDB], CategoryInformation2=[LCDB,MBDB], DataInformation=[UDDB,EQDB,FAME]). The goal is met end to end; no new MCP tool or parameter was added, matching the interface budget of 0.

Two small record notes: the declared after_suite revision (711cfe87a) is one docs-only commit behind the head 818149edb, and the manifest's live-proof.log records 'EDDB manual chunk present: False' while the plan proof names the EDDB manual chunks — the signals section of that same output supplies the required proof.

The out-of-scope surfaces the brief named (imas_codex/llm/server.py tool signatures, the wiki pipeline, scanners) were correctly left untouched. The tests folder used (tests/llm/) is inside the declared tests/search, tests/llm grant.

justifications.durability: The headline behaviour carries a real, non-tautological guard: the per-chunk DOCUMENTS cap has test_stub_chunk_enrichment_query_is_capped, which I falsified independently by removing the slice (all_signals[..$documents_cap] -> all_signals) in a scratch copy at head — exactly that test fails, exit 1, and the unmutated head passes it. But the run's most consequential change, the fulltext parameter rename that revives a branch silently dead behind a bare except, has no regression test: no test references search_query or asserts the bound parameter name, and reverting the rename keeps the 624-test gate green. So the repair is unprotected — the same silent-swallow defect could return unnoticed (see finding 2). The six new tests are otherwise mock-based and exercise the formatter and query-routing paths.
justifications.evidence: Strong and independently reproduced: both gate arms run to their summary line (baseline 618 passed at c323401f9, head 624 passed at 818149edb, both exit 0), the declared negative control reproduces exactly (dropping the per-chunk cap slice makes test_stub_chunk_enrichment_query_is_capped the sole failure, exit 1), and all three live proofs plus a graph census reproduce far from the run's own log. Two qualifications: the reviewed manifest carries baseline_suite=null so the baseline arm is mine, not the run's; and my _search_docs output ranked different documentation chunks than the run's live-proof.log for the same revision (the unrepaired wiki-chunk path makes prose ranking unstable), though the required signals section is present in both.
justifications.fit: The node extends the owners the plan names and the brief's reuse map: _fetch_wiki_page, _enrich_signals and the search_docs/formatter path in imas_codex/llm/, reusing the existing WikiChunk DOCUMENTS edge with no new edge, no new MCP tool and no new parameter. It adds only small module-private helpers and three named caps. The one new enrichment key (documented_pages) and the signals section are the smallest surface that makes the plan's proof true. No abstraction, no sibling module, no interface widening.
justifications.goal_fidelity: §3's MCP done-when is met and independently reproduced live against the jt-60sa graph: fetch of a fronts_database page returns the catalogue it fronts grouped by data class with counts and samples instead of the empty form, search_signals prints the page citation for a DOCUMENTS-linked signal, and search_docs returns the flux-loop signals beside the documentation. The live census corroborates the underlying linkage (6298 signals on CategoryInformation). A point off because the docs-side proof is carried by the CONTAINS fallback rather than the BM25 branch the run also repaired (see the wiki-chunk follow-on), so the documentation ranking is not on its intended path.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff c323401f9..818149edb lists exactly the four declared paths and nothing outside the grant. No plan HTML, facility YAML, schema, sibling scanner or wiki-pipeline file was touched. Commit messages are conventional subjects with bodies and carry no plan/sprint/ticket labels and no AI attribution; symbol and file names describe mechanism, not plan items. The reviewer's own scope is the two review JSON paths.
